# Brew scorecard: floor, predicted setup speed and ladder record, side by side

The ladder is the production test. Per brew, this puts the floor figure, the sim's setup speed and Dustin's ladder record with his three-item setup note in one row. The brew 08 row is first because a prediction about it was written (2026-09-25, about 00:15 CDT) before he played it.

**Standing job of the panel agent (Dustin, Sept 29).** Keep this one file current whenever the Ladder Log changes. It is rewritten in place: no new folder or file per brew.

## How to refresh it

1. Export the Ladder Log's `logs` collection. Read only: never write to the log. Tool ArtifactData, action `list`, url `https://claude.ai/artifact/GHSfGSCzNiWNj8SFPXV3R1`, collection `logs`, query `{"limit": 1000}`, `out_dir` a scratch folder. It writes `<out_dir>/logs/<doc>.json`.
2. From the repo root, in WSL: `python3 decks/screen/panel_ladder_2026-09-26/build_brew_scorecard.py --export <out_dir>`. It rewrites this file. It plays no games and reads no engine.
3. Run it again when a floor page is added or changed under `rl/results/floor*/`, or when `ANCHORS.md` changes. The newest floor page for a deck wins.
4. A Ladder Log doc the script does not know shows up in section E and prints a warning. Add it to `ROWS` in the script if it deserves a row of its own.
5. Do not commit from the panel agent's session unless asked; the parent session reviews and commits.

**Log state at this build:** 56 games in 16 docs with games, record 27-29 (10 wins by concession); newest game filed 2026-09-28 23:43 Chicago time.

Rows are grouped, not ranked. Nothing here ranks the brews, and clearing the floor is not a recommendation (the ranking hold stands).

## What each column is, and is not

- **Floor.** `decks/screen/floor.py`: pilot kog3 on both sides, 240 games against each of the 8 panel decks, 1,920 games in all. Bar: 349 or fewer wins fail, 350-418 are borderline, 419 or more clear. Each matchup is ±6 points, the total ±1.8. It is the sim's win rate against the panel, not a ladder win rate. "Low use" means a flagged card the bot played on under 25% of at least 20 chances, so the sim may understate the deck.
- **Weakest matchups.** The three lowest of the 8, from the floor page.
- **Sim setup.** From the floor page's failure-modes table: the share of games in which the deck's main attacker had made its first attack by the deck's own turn 2, 3 and 4 (your first turn is 1), then the opponent's average points before that attack, for going first (1st) and second (2nd), and the share of games in which it never attacks. "(guess)" means the page had no A1 entry and floor.py took the Pokémon with the highest printed damage as the main attacker.
- **A1 harness.** `decks/consistency_2026-09-25/ANCHORS.md`: points conceded before the deck's first attack of 30+ damage, scripted pilot against `aa`, both seats averaged (± is simulation noise only). Only brews 07-10 have a prediction dated before play. The six anchors' figures are shown for scale: the measure was picked after their ladder results were known.
- **Ladder W-L.** Counted from the Ladder Log export. A concession is a win (Dustin, Sept 28); the number of wins by concession is shown, not adjusted. These are 1 to 10 games: at 10 games a win rate is uncertain by about ±30 points, so it cannot be compared with the floor's percent.
- **Three-item note.** For each game: went first or second, the turn of the first attack with the main attacker, and the opponent's points then. First asked for on Sept 28 (brews 07 and 08), so earlier games have a result and free-text notes only. Items come from the floor page's ladder table when it has one (brew 08's nine video reviews), and from any Note box written as `2nd | Entei T2 | opp 0 pts`. "By T2 x/y" counts games that reached a first attack; games the opponent ended by concession first are left out of y.
- **Three different "opponent points".** A1: scripted pilot against a one-Pokémon goldfish. Floor page: kog3 against kog3 on the panel. Ladder: real opponents. Same idea, different opponents.
